_doc: Revert-verify mutants for vault-exodev ems__Bug 14fb9cb2: ASK honours GROUP BY / HAVING and LIMIT / OFFSET (SPARQL 1.1 §16.3, §18.2.4) — `translateAsk` wraps WHERE in Group (with HAVING) then Slice, and does NOT translate ORDER BY. M8/M9 are the planning review's plausible wrong implementations R1/R2, M10–M17 the specification review's V8/V5/V1–V4/V6/V9, M18–M23 the implementation review's (last GROUP BY variable only, aggregate counter reset per HAVING constraint, DISTINCT before the slice, HAVING without an aggregate as a Filter; round 2: Group on the raw GROUP BY, an empty-pattern shortcut that slices only LIMIT 0) — each passed the harness of its time. `aggregates.length > 0` in the group condition is implied by HAVING here (aggregates come only from HAVING) — kept verbatim from `translateSelect`, so no mutant on it. Each mutant removes one guarantee and must redden exactly the axes in `expect` (pairwise distinct). `red_re` anchors on the jest failure header `● <suite> › <axis> ` (ITRV §A44/§A104). Anchors are CODE lines of `translateAsk` only; the group-condition line repeats in `translateSelect`, so its anchor carries the preceding `modifiers.having` call to stay unique. `tree`/`subject` are placeholders — run the matrix on a copy with the paths substituted (§A145).

M1_no_slice._note: The defect for LIMIT / OFFSET: Slice is not built. A11 is split per path (A11a precondition, A11b run-query, A11c ExoQL.ask, A11d plugin): all four see the missing step. A16 and A17 carry OFFSET forms (3 groups with OFFSET 3; `W OFFSET 2`) that need the slice. A16b (OFFSET 2 over 2 groups) and A20 (OFFSET 3 over 3 duplicate rows) need the slice too. A22 (`GROUP BY (STR(?s)) OFFSET 2`) too.
M1_no_slice.from: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };

M2_no_group._note: The defect for GROUP BY / HAVING: Group is not built. A11 is split per path (A11a precondition, A11b run-query, A11c ExoQL.ask, A11d plugin): all four see the missing step. A15/A15b/A18* use the implicit group (HAVING without GROUP BY); A16 and A17 use GROUP BY with OFFSET / HAVING. A16b slices 3 ungrouped solutions instead of 2 groups; A21 — HAVING dropped, ASK no longer matches SELECT.

M3_slice_before_group._note: Plausible wrong order: Slice goes UNDER Group (cuts solutions, then groups what is left). A17's `WA GROUP BY ?s OFFSET 2` cuts 3 solutions to 1 first and then still finds a group. A16b: OFFSET 2 cuts 3 solutions to 1 first and then still finds a group.
M3_slice_before_group.from: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };
M3_slice_before_group.to: where = where.type === "group" ? { ...where, input: { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where.input } } : { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };

M4_limit_zero_falsy._note: Plausible wrong guard: truthiness instead of `!== undefined` — LIMIT 0 reads as 'no limit'. A11 is split per path (A11a precondition, A11b run-query, A11c ExoQL.ask, A11d plugin): all four see the missing step.

M5_no_implicit_group._note: Plausible wrong guard: Group only with an explicit GROUP BY — HAVING without GROUP BY is dropped. A15/A15b (several HAVING constraints) and A18* (`W0 HAVING (COUNT(*) = 0)`) have no GROUP BY. A21's HAVING has no GROUP BY either, so it is dropped and ASK no longer matches SELECT.

M6_slice_drops_offset._note: Plausible wrong Slice: LIMIT carried, OFFSET lost. A16 (OFFSET 3 over 3 groups) and A17 (`W OFFSET 2`) need OFFSET. A16b (OFFSET 2) and A20 (OFFSET 3) need OFFSET. A22 (OFFSET 2) and A4 (`ASK {} OFFSET 1`) too.
M6_slice_drops_offset.from: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };
M6_slice_drops_offset.to: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, input: where };

M7_orderby_translated._note: ORDER BY translated as for SELECT: the answer is the same (ORDER BY without an aggregate never removes a solution), only the form and the sort cost change — locked by A10 alone.

M8_having_after_slice._note: Plausible wrong order (review R1): HAVING moved ABOVE the slice — groups are cut first, then filtered.
M8_having_after_slice.from: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };
M8_having_after_slice.to:

M9_no_group_on_empty_pattern._note: Plausible wrong guard (review R2): no Group when WHERE is empty — `ASK {}` is one empty solution and groups like any other.

M10_throw_on_slice._note: Review V8: the slice step throws. A button precondition turns the throw into `false`, so only axes that expect `true` on that path (A18a) can see it. Every path that does not catch throws on any LIMIT/OFFSET (C3 carries OFFSET 1 / LIMIT 1 too); A11a stays green — its forms expect `false`, which the catch also gives. A16b, A20 and A21 (`HAVING (1 = 1) LIMIT 1`) carry a slice as well. A22 carries OFFSET too.
M10_throw_on_slice.from: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };

M11_shared_aggregate_state._note: Review V5: the aggregate list and map outlive one translation (instance state, never cleared) — a translator reused across queries (the plugin keeps one) leaks a HAVING aggregate into the next ASK. Only a REUSED translator sees it: A17, and the plugin path A18d (the plugin translator already translated A11d's HAVING query).

M14_having_disjunction._note: Review V3: several HAVING constraints joined by OR instead of AND.
M14_having_disjunction.from:

M16_limit_not_json._note: Review V6: LIMIT carried as a BigInt — breaks only the precondition path's JSON round-trip, whose catch then answers `false`.
M16_limit_not_json.from: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };
M16_limit_not_json.to: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit !== undefined ? (BigInt(modifiers.limit) as unknown as number) : undefined, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };

M18_last_group_variable._note: Implementation review: only the LAST GROUP BY variable is kept (mirror of M15). A16 cannot see it — there the last variable ?a determines ?s; A16b groups by (?s, ?c) with a constant ?c.
M18_last_group_variable.from:
variables: groupVars,
        aggregates,
        having: havingExpressions.length > 0 ? havingExpressions : undefined,
        input: where,
M18_last_group_variable.to:

M19_counter_reset_per_having._note: Implementation review: the aggregate counter is reset for every HAVING constraint, so two DIFFERENT aggregates get the same name and one overwrites the other. A15/A15b repeat one COUNT(*) and cannot see it; A15c pairs COUNT with MAX.

M20_distinct_before_slice._note: Implementation review: duplicate solutions removed before the slice. No other fixture has duplicate solutions; A20 slices a projecting subquery that keeps 3 rows of 2 subjects.
M20_distinct_before_slice.from: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: where };
M20_distinct_before_slice.to: where = { type: "slice", limit: modifiers.limit, offset: modifiers.offset, input: { type: "distinct", input: where } };

M21_having_no_aggregate_as_filter._note: Implementation review (R3 of the planning review): HAVING without an aggregate and without GROUP BY translated as a Filter. Correct by SPARQL 1.1, but ASK then disagrees with SELECT, whose shared grouping step builds a group (ems__Bug 2653916f) — parity is the design, locked by A21.

M22_group_on_raw_group_by._note: Implementation review round 2 (V31): Group built from the RAW `GROUP BY` instead of the translated variables. GROUP BY by an expression yields no variable today (ems__Bug 38328fcc), so the solutions collapse into ONE group — `GROUP BY (STR(?s)) OFFSET 1` answers false, worse than the base. Locked by the absolute axis A22.

M23_empty_pattern_limit_zero_only._note: Implementation review round 2 (V39): a shortcut for the empty pattern that slices only LIMIT 0 — `ASK {} OFFSET 1` then answers true. A4 carries OFFSET forms over `{}`.
